summary.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 132 crore, down 6% YoY, with digital down about 17% to INR 56 crore and traditional up 5% to INR 76 crore. EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore versus INR 56 crore a year earlier, after about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend; excluding that, existing operations EBITDA was about INR 18 crore. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. Management said this is the first quarter after the inventory charge-off exercise, now in a normal charge-off cycle, and guided to double-digit blended growth, EBITDA-positive for the year, and bottom-line positive next year.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of approx. INR 56 crore (call analyst cited 55.5 crore) in Q1 FY26
materially reduced YoY; no prior figure stated

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 56 crore, down 17% YoY, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on geopolitical uncertainty; consumer business grew on fresh content and ad monetisation. Management targets double-digit digital growth.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 76 crore, up 5% YoY, helped by closure of B2B licensing deals that offset subdued ad environment. Management expects roughly flat traditional revenue for FY27, with near-term ad outlook subdued due to BARC ratings blackout.

segments.name: ShemarooMe (OTT, Gujarati)
segments.commentary: Acquired OHO Gujarati catalogue in April 2026 (over 22 Gujarati originals); released 10 new titles in the quarter. Company does not disclose subscriber, ARPU or revenue figures; management said it is about two years from OTT profitability.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Approx. 9 billion views across channels in the quarter; Shemaroo Filmi Gaane passed 74.7 million subscribers and Shemaroo Entertainment 61.9 million. Management said views are seasonal but viewership share remains strong.

guidance_outlook: Blended revenue growth aim of healthy double digits over the next 2-3 years; digital targeted at double-digit growth, outpacing recent low-double-digit industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
Traditional media revenue expected flattish for FY27, not declining.
Aim for EBITDA-positive for full FY27 (conservative view); management expects bottom-line positive next year (FY28).
Debt reduction plan for FY27, but no quantified target given; quarterly fluctuations possible given geopolitical and BARC blackout impacts.
Aspiration of around 20% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years, not a committed target; management said it is not sure it will be achieved.
New-initiative spend to be cut by more than 50% in FY27 versus FY26; management said the company is on track.
capex_capacity: Content strategy shifted: new content creation scaled down in traditional, while new content acquisition is being scaled up in digital.
Traditional channel rationalisation possible; company now runs two FAST channels after earlier shrinking the number.
OTT (ShemarooMe) needs ongoing content and customer-acquisition spend (ATL, BTL and performance marketing); management said little upfront capex is needed.
Inventory of INR 348 crore at Q1 end; management said no remaining write-down risk and the company is now in a normal charge-off cycle.
demand_pricing: Digital decline attributed to deferred B2B syndication deals (geopolitical uncertainty) and lumpy B2B revenue; consumer digital grew on fresh content and better ad monetisation.
Traditional ad market subdued for a long period; BARC ratings blackout in recent month has hit traditional and syndication revenue.
Acquired content is priced competitively against other bidders, so new-content margins are lower than on legacy content already amortised or charged off.
YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved meaningfully; company is focusing on connected-TV long-form content, and is only experimenting with micro-dramas.
FAST channel ecosystem globally has been shrinking for roughly 12-18 months; company is tracking it and scaling only if monetisation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA excluding the new-initiative investment, and what revenue is needed for positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend, EBITDA would have been about INR 18 crore. Management said margin depends on both revenue growth and cost cuts, and on revenue mix, so it would not give a revenue threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no under-utilisation, citing 9 billion views in the quarter. Traditional monetisation is declining while digital is growing. The aim is healthy double-digit blended growth, outdoing digital industry growth by a couple of points.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: A debt reduction plan exists for FY27 but no figure was given. EBITDA-positive for the year is the conservative aim, with bottom-line positive next year. Digital is seen at double-digit growth and traditional roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry underlying growth was low, and it would not burn cash to grow faster, since that would strain cash flow and the balance sheet. It cited its leadership in Gujarati entertainment.

qa_highlights.question: Which digital segments carry the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on content age, not platform. Legacy content can yield 80-90% margins, newly acquired content can be near zero or negative, and production work can earn 10-20%. YouTube is not inherently high-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin, and is 20% EBITDA the aim on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not satisfied with current margins and aspires to upwards of 20% EBITDA in 2-3 years. It declined to say whether this is on a reported basis net of all investments, and said the structural shift in the media industry is a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and inventory at quarter end, and is further write-down likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was INR 311 crore and inventory INR 348 crore at quarter end. Management said the company is in a normal charge-off cycle with no further rationalisation planned.

qa_highlights.question: How long until ShemarooMe reaches break-even, and will it disclose subscriber or revenue data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is about two years from OTT break-even. It does not disclose DAU, MAU, subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue, and said it has no current plan to start.

risks_watch: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY on deferred B2B syndication deals; lumpy B2B timing could keep quarterly digital revenue volatile.
Traditional ad market remains weak and BARC ratings blackout is hurting traditional and syndication revenue.
Debt of INR 311 crore against an EBITDA-positive-for-year aim; quarterly debt movements may vary.
Limited disclosure: no OTT subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue data, and no quantified debt target; analysts asked for more granularity.
YouTube Shorts and micro-drama monetisation still unproven; a possible YouTube monetisation policy update was not confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating trajectory and cost discipline, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give debt targets, OTT data, profitability timing, or a revenue threshold for breakeven. It acknowledged margins are below its own aspiration.
key_quotes: Every quarter, I think we should be seeing an improvement on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Are we satisfied with it? Definitely not.
I think if I see a 2 -3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

growth.why: Management aims for healthy double-digit blended revenue growth over 2-3 years (digital double-digit, traditional flattish in FY27) and EBITDA-positive FY27, with EBITDA loss narrowing to about INR 2 crore; backing is qualitative (content acquisition, B2B deal recovery, cut in new-initiative spend by over 50%) with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA improved from a loss of about INR 56 crore to about INR -2 crore, and ex the INR 20 crore new-initiative spend it was about INR 18 crore; new-initiative spend is to be cut by more than 50% in FY27, and management guides to EBITDA-positive for FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; content creation is being scaled down in traditional, and FAST channels were shrunk to two, so no new capacity is planned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets digital double-digit growth and healthy double-digit blended growth over 2-3 years, though digital fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore in Q1 and traditional is guided flattish for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says little upfront capex is needed for OTT and the company is in a normal charge-off cycle; capex was not discussed beyond content spend.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is conservative on EBITDA-positive (described as a conservative aim), and the Q1 revenue fell 6% YoY, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore on lumpy B2B syndication deals, the traditional ad market is weak with a BARC ratings blackout, and quarterly fluctuations were flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ten new ShemarooMe titles were released in Q1 and the OHO Gujarati catalogue (over 22 originals) was acquired in April 2026, so ongoing content launches are firmly under way, though no new brand or platform launch was named.

rows.label: New-initiative spend cut by over 50% in FY27
rows.why: New-initiative spend was about INR 20 crore in Q1 and management says it is on track to cut it by more than 50% versus FY26, which is the main driver of the EBITDA turn.

rows.label: Debt reduction plan for FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed a debt reduction plan for this year, but gave no amount, against total debt of INR 311 crore at quarter end.

rows.label: Inventory charge-off cycle normalised
rows.why: Management says no remaining write-down risk and a normal charge-off cycle now applies against INR 348 crore of inventory, which should stop the large write-downs that drove last year's losses.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline, the EBITDA turn and content library strength, but evasive on debt targets, OTT subscriber data, profitability timing and a breakeven revenue threshold, and admitted margins are below its aspiration; analysts pressed on granularity and the path to profitab
